reason: Shading the lower tail of the distribution of the sample mean shows why 96.5 is unusual for a mean of 16 times but not for one rower.

scenes.title: Where does a sample mean of 96.5 sit?
scenes.purpose: See that the mean of 16 times has a much narrower distribution than a single time, so 96.5 falls in the lower 5% tail and the null hypothesis is rejected.

steps.text: Under $H_0: \mu = 98$ (with $H_1: \mu < 98$) the mean of 16 times follows a narrow curve centred on $98$. The dashed curve is a single rower, $\mathrm{N}(98, 3.2^2)$. This is the B1 for the hypotheses.

The mean of 16 times has standard deviation $\frac{3.2}{\sqrt{16}} = 0.8$, so the solid curve is much narrower than the dashed one. This is the M1; using the dashed curve instead is the sample-mean-sd-not-scaled pitfall.

Set the slider to $96.5$. The standardised value is $z = \frac{96.5-98}{0.8} = -1.875$, and the shaded lower tail reads about $0.0304$. This is the A1 for the probability; the green line marks the 5% cut-off at about $96.68$.

Drag the slider towards $98$: the shaded area passes $0.05$ when the mean reaches about $96.68$. Since $96.5$ is below this, $0.0304 < 0.05$, so you reject $H_0$ and conclude that there is evidence the new plan has lowered the mean 500 m time. This is the final A1.

guide.what_you_see: Two bell curves centred on $98$: a narrow solid one for the mean $\bar{T}$ of 16 juniors' times and a wide dashed one for a single rower's time $T$. A vertical line marks your observed sample mean, and the area to its left under the narrow curve is shaded.

legend.meaning: The distribution of the sample mean $\bar{T}$ of 16 times under $\mathrm{H}_0$: $\mathrm{N}\left(98, \frac{3.2^2}{16}\right)$, standard deviation $0.8$ (labelled 'mean of 16').
The dashed distribution of a single rower's time, $T \sim \mathrm{N}(98, 3.2^2)$ (labelled 'one rower'); much wider than $f$.
The shaded lower-tail area under $f$ from the left edge up to the slider value $m$; this is $\mathrm{P}(\bar{T} < m)$, the probability your decision is based on.
The green vertical line at about $96.684$, the 5% cut-off: the area to its left under $f$ is $0.05$.
The vertical line at the observed sample mean $m$ set by the slider.

interact.do: Drag the slider between $94$ and $98$, first setting it to $96.5$, then sliding it towards $98$ and back.
interact.watch: At $m=96.5$ the shaded area reads about $0.0304$ (corresponding to $z=-1.875$). As $m$ rises the area grows, and it passes $0.05$ as the line $obs$ crosses the green cut-off near $96.68$; at $m=98$ it is $0.5$.

question_link.text: The solid curve $f$ is the distribution of $\bar{T}$ under $\mathrm{H}_0: \mu=98$ with standard deviation $0.8$ (the B1 and M1 steps), and the shaded area to the left of the observed mean $96.5$ is the $\mathrm{P}(\bar{T}<96.5)\approx 0.0304$ of the A1. Seeing it lie beyond the green 5% cut-off, so $0.0304<0.05$, shows why $\mathrm{H}_0$ is rejected in the final A1.

'Shaded area = …' shows $\mathrm{P}(\bar{T}<m)$ under $\mathrm{N}(98,0.8^2)$; at $m=96.5$ it is about $0.0304$, to compare with the significance level $0.05$.
